documents.title: Emergency Department Record (received 2026-07-22)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 7/6/2026.

CC: SOB, cough, R-sided chest pain.

HPI: 52M with COPD and HTN, five days of worsening dyspnea and a cough bringing up yellow sputum, with sharp right chest pain on deep breaths. Has felt feverish at home, not measured high. Still smoking.

PMH: COPD, HTN. PSH: appendectomy. Home meds: tiotropium 18 mcg daily, albuterol 90 mcg prn, amlodipine 5 mg daily. NKDA. FH: father COPD, mother HTN. SH: construction, current smoker 35 pk-yr, occasional EtOH.

Triage: T 38.3, BP 135/85, HR 102, RR 22, SpO2 92% RA.

Exam: ill appearing, mildly tachypneic. Right base dull to percussion with decreased breath sounds. Left lung clear. Tachycardic, regular. No leg edema.

CXR: right-sided effusion.

Bedside US-guided diagnostic thoracentesis, right: cloudy fluid. Pleural fluid pH 7.1, glucose 40, WBC 60,000 with 90% PMNs. Gram stain gram-positive cocci in clusters.

MDM: pneumonia with complicated parapneumonic effusion, sepsis. Blood cultures x2 drawn. Ceftriaxone and azithromycin IV, vancomycin added after the Gram stain. IV fluids. Pulmonary/ICU consulted; right-sided small-bore chest tube placed by the ICU team, purulent drainage, to suction. Oxygen requirement climbing through the morning.

Disposition: admitted to the ICU.

documents.title: ICU Admission Note, 7/6/2026 (received 2026-07-22)
documents.author: pulmonary and critical care
documents.body:
Medical ICU admission, 7/6/2026, late afternoon.

52-year-old man with COPD and hypertension seen in our ED this morning with a complicated right parapneumonic effusion, chest tube in place. Over the day his work of breathing and oxygen needs escalated; intubated for hypoxemic respiratory failure and placed on the ventilator.

Initial vent: VT 10 mL/kg PBW, RR 16, PEEP 8. BP 110/70, HR 102, SpO2 88%.
Exam: sedated, intubated. Crackles both lung fields. Chest tube draining pus to suction.
ABG: 7.32 / 50 / 68, HCO3 24. Lactate 2.2. P/F 150.
CXR: diffuse bilateral infiltrates.

Home meds tiotropium, albuterol, amlodipine. NKDA.

Impression: moderate ARDS from pneumonia with complicated parapneumonic effusion; sepsis.
Plan: lung-protective ventilation, drop tidal volume toward 6 mL/kg and titrate PEEP; continue ceftriaxone, azithromycin and vancomycin pending cultures; hold amlodipine; bronchoscopy with lavage in the morning to look for other organisms; conservative fluids as pressure allows.

documents.title: ICU Progress Note, 7/8/2026 (received 2026-07-22)
documents.author: pulmonary and critical care
documents.body:
MICU day 2, 7/8/2026.

Oxygenation still poor despite FiO2 0.8 and PEEP 12 at VT 6 mL/kg IBW. ABG 7.32 / 45 / 68, HCO3 22, so P/F about 85: refractory hypoxemia. Urine output down to 20 mL/h over the past 6 hours. Weight up 3 kg since admission.

Vitals: BP 95/60 on norepinephrine, HR 110, RR 28 on the vent, T 38.3.
Exam: crackles throughout both lungs. 2+ pitting edema of both lower extremities.
Labs: Cr 1.8 (baseline 1.0), BUN 36, Na 145, K 4.5. Hgb 9.8, WBC 18,000, plt 250,000.
CXR: diffuse bilateral infiltrates unchanged.
Micro: pleural fluid growing Staph aureus, methicillin-susceptible. Blood cultures no growth so far. BAL from yesterday pending.

Current: ceftriaxone, azithromycin, vancomycin, norepinephrine.

A/P: ARDS with refractory hypoxemia, sepsis from MSSA empyema.
- Prone positioning starting today.
- Stop vancomycin and ceftriaxone, start cefazolin IV for MSSA. Azithromycin to finish its course.
- Norepinephrine to MAP goal. Diuresis once pressors are off.
- Creatinine up from baseline with low urine output; avoid nephrotoxins, dose drugs to kidney function.
- Chest tube to suction.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary (received 2026-07-22)
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Admitted 7/6/2026, discharged 7/21/2026.

Principal diagnosis: complicated right parapneumonic effusion (MSSA empyema).
Other diagnoses this admission: ARDS with refractory hypoxemia requiring mechanical ventilation; sepsis. Chronic: COPD, hypertension.

Course:
Presented 7/6 with five days of dyspnea, productive cough and right pleuritic pain, febrile and hypoxic. Thoracentesis showed a complicated effusion (pH 7.1, glucose 40, WBC 60,000, GPC in clusters). Right chest tube placed in the ED on 7/6 with purulent drainage. Intubated the same afternoon for hypoxemic respiratory failure; ARDS. Pleural culture grew methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus; blood cultures were negative.

Bronchoscopy with BAL 7/7: bacterial culture grew the same S. aureus. Fungal culture, Pneumocystis PCR, AFB smear and culture all negative. No opportunistic infection identified.

Refractory hypoxemia on 7/8 managed with low tidal volume ventilation, higher PEEP and prone positioning 7/8 to 7/10. Norepinephrine for sepsis-related hypotension, off 7/10. Ceftriaxone and vancomycin changed to IV cefazolin on 7/8; azithromycin completed 7/10. After pressors came off he was diuresed. Creatinine peaked at 1.8 with low urine output and returned to 1.1 by discharge. Extubated 7/13. Chest tube removed 7/16. Worked with PT, walking the halls on room air by discharge.

At discharge: SpO2 93% on room air at rest. Hgb 10.4, Cr 1.1. CXR 7/20 improving bilateral infiltrates with small residual right pleural fluid.

Discharge medications:
- cephalexin 500 mg by mouth four times daily through 8/5/2026
- nicotine patch 21 mg/24 h daily
- tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily (continue)
- albuterol 90 mcg inhaled as needed (continue)
- HOLD amlodipine 5 mg: blood pressure low normal here; PCP to decide on restarting.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: pulmonary clinic in 3 weeks with chest x-ray. PCP within 1 to 2 weeks.
Smoking: counseled; agreeable to the patch.

documents.title: Hospital records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: ED record, ICU notes, micro and imaging, and discharge summary from his 7/6 to 7/21 admission are in. MSSA empyema with ARDS, intubated a week, chest tube, home on cephalexin through 8/5 and a nicotine patch, amlodipine on hold. RN to call him and get a post-hospital visit on the books.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Spoke with patient, two days home. Tired, short of breath with stairs, better than in the hospital. No fever. Taking cephalexin four times a day, has the patch on. Using tiotropium; albuterol a few times a day. Not taking amlodipine, per the hospital.

Offered a post-hospital visit with PCP this week or next. He would rather wait until after the lung clinic visit on 8/11 and will call us after that to set a time. Reviewed reasons to call or go to the ED: fever, worse breathing, chest pain. He verbalized understanding.

documents.title: Pulmonary Clinic Letter (received 2026-08-13)
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary group. Visit 8/11/2026.

Dear colleague,

I saw Mr. Dupuis three weeks after his discharge following MSSA empyema complicated by ARDS and sepsis, with a week on the ventilator. He has a few days of cephalexin left. Energy is coming back; he still gets winded on a flight of stairs. No fevers, sputum minimal. He is down to a few cigarettes a day with the nicotine patch, which I encouraged.

SpO2 94% on room air at rest, BP 128/78 off amlodipine. Lungs with decreased breath sounds at the right base, no crackles. Healed chest tube site.

Chest x-ray today: infiltrates largely cleared, mild residual right pleural thickening.

Plan:
1. Finish cephalexin as prescribed.
2. Repeat chest x-ray in 6 to 8 weeks.
3. Full pulmonary function testing in about 3 months, once recovered.
4. Continue tiotropium and albuterol.
5. I have left the amlodipine decision to you.

Meds: tiotropium 18 mcg daily, albuterol prn, cephalexin 500 mg four times daily, nicotine patch 21 mg. Amlodipine on hold. NKDA.

Thank you for letting us share his care.

documents.title: Time to come in
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Keith, I got the letter from the lung clinic, glad you're on the mend. I'd like to see you in the office soon to go over your blood pressure medicine and how you're recovering. Please book any open slot, or reply and we'll find one.
